Class GTNetBodySizeFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
grafiosch.m2m.rest.GTNetBodySizeFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanNameAware, org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, org.springframework.context.EnvironmentAware, org.springframework.core.env.EnvironmentCapable, org.springframework.web.context.ServletContextAware
@Component public class GTNetBodySizeFilter extends org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
The outer bound on an inbound M2M request body.

No Spring Boot property caps a JSON body: server.max-http-request-header-size is headers only, server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size applies to form encoding and spring.servlet.multipart.max-request-size to multipart. The cap therefore lives in a filter, ahead of the message converter, so an over-sized body is refused before Jackson materializes it into memory.

The refusal is HTTP 200 with a GNetCoreMessageCode.GT_NET_ERROR_S envelope rather than HTTP 413, for the same reason the endpoint carries no @Valid: BaseDataClient discards the body of every non-2xx, so a 413 would reach the sender as a failed delivery with no reason. The envelope is written as a literal, because a filter runs outside any transaction and an error path must not need the database.
